ledger.x: 1429: Shō Hashi unites Okinawa as the Ryukyu Kingdom.
1429: Shō Hashi moves the capital from Urasoe to Shuri Castle.
1429: the unified kingdom is a Ming tributary.
1447: Amami Ōshima is conquered.
1470: Shō En founds the Second Shō dynasty.
1500: the Sakishima Islands (the Miyako and Yaeyama groups) are annexed.
1609: Satsuma lands in the Ryukyus.
1609: Shuri Castle falls.
1609: the Ryukyu Kingdom becomes a vassal of the Satsuma Domain.
1611: Satsuma annexes the Amami Islands.
1644: the Ming dynasty ends and the tributary status passes to the Southern Ming.
1644: the kingdom is recorded as a tributary of the Southern Ming.
1646: the Southern Ming status ends.
1646: the kingdom becomes a tributary of the Qing.
1872: the Qing tributary status ends in the infobox ('Tributary state of the Qing dynasty (1646–1872)').
1872: the Satsuma vassalage ends as Japan reorganizes the kingdom as the Ryukyu Domain.
1872: Meiji Japan declares the kingdom the Ryukyu Domain.
1872: the kingdom becomes a domain of the Empire of Japan.
1879: Japan abolishes the Ryukyu Domain and incorporates the islands as Okinawa Prefecture, ending the domain status; the land passes to direct Japanese rule (the dissolve below).
1879: Japan abolishes the Ryukyu Domain and annexes the islands as Okinawa Prefecture.

wars.name: Oyake Akahachi Rebellion
wars.outcome: The page's timeline lists the Sakishima Islands as annexed in 1500; the rebellion's course and end are not stated on the page.

wars.name: Shō Toku's attacks on Kikai Island
wars.outcome: 'In 1466, King Shō Toku attacked Kikai Island on two occasions'; the page does not state the result.

wars.name: Suppression of Onikō's rebellion on Yonaguni
wars.outcome: 'In 1522, he suppressed the rebellion of Onikō in Yonaguni'; a revolt put down inside the kingdom, not a new conquest.

wars.name: Invasion of Ryukyu
wars.outcome: Satsuma victory: Shuri Castle was entered on 5 May 1609, King Shō Nei was taken to Kagoshima and Edo, surrender documents were signed in 1611 and the Amami Islands were annexed by Satsuma; the kingdom stayed nominally independent under Satsuma control, in…

certainty.note: An island group with approximate extents: the dates of the Amami (1447) and Sakishima (1500: the Miyako and Yaeyama groups) additions are the page's, the outline of each is a gazetteer region, and the Kume addition is undated on the pages.
Satsuma 'conducted land surveys of all the islands' after 1611 and the peace treaty fixed the Amami annexation; the Okinawa-Amami line is the treaty line.
